source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.14
text: The manual describes a simple method for producing rice-husk charcoal (ធ្យូងអង្កាម), which is used as a cover/mulch material for nursery/germination beds. Using a metal chimney pipe set inside a perforated drum or barrel: (1) set up the chimney and drum. (2) Start a small fire of kindling inside the drum. (3) Once the fire is confirmed burning well, (4) heap rice husk around and over the chimney/drum. (5) Cover the husk pile completely. (6) The husk smolders and chars over roughly a day, producing charcoal without an open flame. (7–8) Once charring/smoking has finished, the smoldering husk is doused with water to stop combustion and fully carbonize it (avoid letting it burn to white ash, which is not usable). (9) The finished rice-husk charcoal is collected, dried, and stored for use as a nursery-bed dressing/cover material.
